howItWorks.intro: Every two months the practice turns one idea into a working tool. In the Blueprint month you share ideas, vote on a shortlist of three, and the winner is scoped; in the Build month two builders ship it and play it back to everyone.

steps.title: Share an idea
steps.summary: The idea form is always open, so anyone in the practice can submit an idea at any time.
steps.detail: Fill in three fields in under a minute: your idea in one line, the problem it solves and for whom, and your name if you want credit. No GitHub account or login is needed. The builders ask for any missing detail in the Slack thread later.

steps.title: Triage in 30 minutes
steps.summary: The two builders score every new idea in one short session.
steps.detail: Each idea is scored from 1 to 5 on impact, feasibility, reusability and showcase value, with impact and feasibility counting double. The data check is pass or fail: only internal, public or synthetic data gets through. The top three become the shortlist.

steps.title: Vote in Slack
steps.summary: The practice picks the winner from the shortlist of three with a reaction emoji in Slack.
steps.detail: Voting stays open for 5 working days in the Slack channel, with one reminder and a mention on the practice call. The idea with the most reactions wins, and ties go to the higher feasibility score. Runners-up stay in the backlog and are shortlisted again automatically next cycle, once. Results and turnout are published on this site.

steps.title: Scope it with the owner
steps.summary: The winning idea is scoped with the person who suggested it.
steps.detail: The builders and the idea owner agree what a demoable slice looks like, and anything that does not fit is logged as v2. The aim is something two builders can finish in about 6 person-days.

steps.title: Build it
steps.summary: Two builders build the winner across the first three weeks of the Build month.
steps.detail: The build takes about 6 person-days, shared by the two builders. The idea owner is invited to test it first, and anything unfinished is cut back to a slice that can be demoed.

steps.title: Ship and MVP Drop
steps.summary: The MVP ships with docs and a demo video, then is played back live to the practice.
steps.detail: In the fourth week the builders test it, write the README and record a demo video. At the start of the next cycle it is played back in a 20-minute MVP Drop, then added to the catalog as Live, and the next round of ideas opens.

rules.title: About 6 person-days
rules.text: An MVP has to be buildable in about 6 person-days, shared by two builders across the Build month.

rules.title: Demoable in 5 minutes
rules.text: If it cannot be shown working in 5 minutes, it is too big or too vague for one cycle.

rules.title: No client data
rules.text: Internal, public or synthetic data only. Ideas that need client data do not pass the data check at triage.

rules.title: Approved tools only
rules.text: MVPs use approved tools and AI services only.

rules.title: Shipped as is
rules.text: Every MVP is documented and has an owner, but comes with no support commitment. Feedback goes to the Slack channel.

rules.title: Bigger ideas wait
rules.text: Anything bigger goes to a Productionise shortlist (a longer-term list for bigger ideas that deserve proper investment), not the Build month.

faq.q: What counts as an MVP here?
faq.a: A small working tool that two builders can make in about 6 person-days and demo in 5 minutes. It can be a script, a tool hosted on an internal platform, a spreadsheet or Power BI file, or a Claude skill.
Anyone in the practice. The form is always open and takes under a minute. Your name is optional, but giving it means the idea owner gets the credit.

faq.q: Do I need a GitHub account?
faq.a: No. Ideas go in through the form on this site, you vote with a reaction in Slack, and every download in the catalog is a single zip file.

faq.q: What happens to ideas that don't win?
faq.a: Runners-up stay in the backlog and are shortlisted again automatically in the next cycle, once. The best idea that did not win can also get an idea of the cycle shout-out.
Internal, public or synthetic data only. Never client data. The data check at triage is pass or fail, so an idea that needs client data cannot reach the shortlist.
No. MVPs are shipped as is: documented and owned, but with no support commitment. Send feedback to the Slack channel. Each MVP is reviewed every 6 months and retired if nobody uses it.

faq.q: How do I install a Claude skill?
faq.a: Download the skill's zip from the Claude Skills page, then upload it in the Claude app, copy it into Claude Code's skills folder, or ask your organisation owner to provision it. The How to install panel on that page has the steps.
Yes, ask in the Slack channel. The aim is for one volunteer to join each Build month as a guest builder, to learn alongside the two regular builders.

points: Voting stays open for 5 working days, with one reminder in the channel and a mention on the practice call.

The idea with the most reactions wins.

install.intro: A skill is a folder with a SKILL.md file that teaches Claude a repeatable task. Download its zip from the card, then use whichever of these fits how you work.

steps.title: Claude app
steps.text: Download the zip. In Claude, go to Customize > Skills and choose Upload a skill, then pick the zip. Skills you upload are private to you.

steps.title: Claude Code
steps.text: Unzip the download. The unzipped folder that contains SKILL.md is the skill folder (skill-folder in the commands below). Copy it into ~/.claude/skills/ to use it in every project, or into .claude/skills/ inside one repo (run those two commands from that repo's folder) to use it there only.
steps.code:
# for all your projects
mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills
cp -r skill-folder ~/.claude/skills/

# for one repo only
mkdir -p .claude/skills
cp -r skill-folder .claude/skills/

steps.title: Team or Enterprise plans
steps.text: Ask your Claude organisation owner to provision the practice skills organisation-wide. They then appear for everyone, with no uploading.
